THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:14/10/2010 PASSED IN MVC  NO.2712/2008 ON THE FILE OF THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:21429  MFA No. 8433 of 2011 TRIBUNAL, VII ADDL.
JUDGE, MEMBER, MACT-3, BANGALORE,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS M.F.A., COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 14.10.2010 passed in MVC.No.2712/2008 by the learned VII Additional Judge and Member, MACT-III (Court of Small Causes, SCCH-2), Bengaluru, seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2.
Brief facts of the case are that, on 21.01.2008, the claimant was riding motor cycle along with his wife as pillion rider.

At about 7.15 p.m., on the road leading to Holur to Yeldur, when they reached the place in between Yeduru-Chintamakalahalli Village, at that time, a Tata Sumo Maxi Cab bearing Reg. No.KA-01/ED-4353 came in high speed and rash and negligent manner, due to which, he lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the motor cycle and as a result, the motor cycle and the NC: 2023:KHC:21429 claimant fell down and he claimant sustained grievous injuries.
3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl. Head of compensation Amount/Rs.
No . 1

Pain and sufferings 50,000/- 2 Loss of amenities and 50,000/-
future unhappiness 3

Medical expenses 1,55,703/-
4

Incidental expenses like 10,000/-
nourishment, attendant and conveyance 5 Future Medical expenses 10,000/-
6 Reduction of Span life 30,000/-

2  Total 3,05,703/-
 5.

Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by NC: 2023:KHC:21429 the Tribunal is meager one and prays for enhancement of compensation by allowing the present appeal.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company justifying the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. In the present case, from the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant has suffered bycondylar fracture of right tibia, injury to right arm, right knee and other grievous injuries all over the body.
His movement is restricted about 30 degree of flexion out of 140 degree and has suffered mal-united lateral condylar fracture with sign of osteoarthritis of right knee.

8. Therefore, considering the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation granted under the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities and future unhappiness' and 'medical expenses' are found to be just and proper.
Hence, they are not disturbed and the same remained in tact.
The compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'future medical expenses' is found to be on lower side.
The evidence on record proves that the claimant had undergone three surgeries.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.35,000/- under the head 'future medical expenses' is awarded.

10. The Tribunal has not granted compensation under the head 'future loss of income' or 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' even though the claimant had suffered physical disability of 45%
to the right lower limb and 15% to the whole body.
But, during the course of cross-examination, the doctor admitted that the claimant had suffered physical disability towards whole body at 36%.
The claimant is a electric contractor by profession.
Therefore, certainly this disability affects the earning capacity of the claimant.
11. Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the disability occurred, as per the doctor's evidence the functional disability is taken as 6%.

The accident was NC: 2023:KHC:21429 occurred in the year 2008 and the income tax returns shows that the claimant was earning gross income of Rs.3,00,000/- p.a., by doing electric contract work that will come to Rs.25,000/- p.m., as gross income.
The net income would be taken as 40%, it comes to Rs.10,000/- (40% of Rs.25,000).
Therefore, the net income would be considered as Rs.10,000/- per month.
The claimant was aged 45 years old as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier is '14'.
Therefore, "loss of future income due to disability/loss of earning capacity" is hereby assessed as Rs.10,000X6/100X14X12= 1,00,800/-.

sentences.text: Further, the Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head 'loss of income during the laid up period'.
Due to the injuries sustained, the claimant is unable to attend his work.

Accordingly,
Rs.20,000/- (10,000X2) is awarded under the head "loss of income during laid up period".

Further, the compensation granted under the head 'reduction of span of life' at Rs.30,000/- is amounting to double claim/compensation, since the claimant is granted compensation under the head 'loss of income due to disability'.
Therefore, Rs.30,000/- is to be deducted.
Hence, the amount of Rs.30,000/- granted by the Tribunal under the head 'reduction of span of life', is hereby set aside.

14. Thus in all, the appellant/claimant is entitled to the compensation as follows:
Sl. Head of compensation Amount/Rs. No. 1 Injury, Pain and suffering 50,000.00 2 Loss of amenities and 50,000.00 future unhappiness 3

Medical Expenses 1,55,703.00 4 Future Medical Expenses 35,000.00 5 Loss of income during laid 20,000.00 up period 6 Loss of Future Income due 1,00,800.00 to disability/Loss of Earning Capacity NC: 2023:KHC:21429 Total 4,11,503.00 (Less) Reduction of Span life (-) 30.000.00
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,05,703/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,81,503/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.75,800/- (Rs.3,81,503 - Rs.3,05,703) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

16. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.2712/2008 dated 14.10.2010, is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.75,800/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from NC: 2023:KHC:21429 the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The appellant/claimant is not entitled for the interest for the delayed period of 178 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
 v. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order forthwith without any delay.
vi. Draw award accordingly.
